data.description:
## Observation
The force-close hint advertises a no-force path for administrative dispositions:
> Hint: if this close is administrative (duplicate / obsolete / superseded / wontfix rather than completed work), --class <value> closes it through the attested disposition path — obsolete/wontfix with --reason=<text> ... no --force needed.

But in practice on ticket 192c-d606-b72e-470f (brokendown-graceless-pelican, task, invalid premise per ADR 0107):
1. `rebar transition <id> open closed --class obsolete --reason=...` fails: 'plan-review close gate: unsigned: no certified plan-review attestation. Run rebar review-plan ... then retry close.'
2. Running review-plan produces a signed BLOCK (correctly — the premise is invalid), which does NOT satisfy the gate.
3. Retrying the administrative close fails identically.

So a ticket whose premise is invalid can NEVER be closed without operator --force: the only attestation the gate accepts is a PASSING plan review, which an invalid-premise ticket can never earn. This has now trapped two tickets (bairnly-elliptic-toad b735-788d-72eb-411f, brokendown-graceless-pelican 192c-d606-b72e-470f); both required operator force, which the workflow treats as break-glass.

## Hypothesis
The attested-disposition path for administrative close classes should accept a signed plan-review verdict of EITHER polarity (or mint its own disposition attestation from the --class + --reason + a currency check), rather than requiring a certified PASSING plan-review attestation that is definitionally unobtainable for obsolete/invalid-premise tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An open task/bug with a signed BLOCK (or no review at all) can be closed with --class obsolete/wontfix/duplicate/superseded + --reason (+ live replacement link where the class requires one) WITHOUT --force, and the close records a signed disposition attestation naming the class and reason.
- [ ] Completed-work closes (no --class, or completion classes) keep the existing certified plan-review + completion-verifier requirements unchanged.
- [ ] The hint text and docs/plan-review-gate.md accurately describe the behavior.
- [ ] Regression test: reproduce the pelican sequence (create ticket, signed BLOCK review, administrative close succeeds without force; completion close still gated).
data.title: Administrative close (--class obsolete/wontfix) still demands plan-review attestation, contradicting its own hint
